newsitem.title: UK: Jamaica, New Zealand, Denmark tap dollar Eurobonds.
newsitem.headline: Jamaica, New Zealand, Denmark tap dollar Eurobonds.

text.p: Sovereign borrowers provided the main activity in the Eurobond market on Thursday.
Jamaica issued its debut Eurobond transaction, raising $200 million via a five-year bond. The deal will be priced later to yield between 330 and 340 basis points over U.S. Treasury notes.
Bankers familiar with the transaction said the deal was oversubscribed, and the strong demand allowed Jamaica to raise double the amount originally mooted.
Jamaica is not rated, but bankers said the pricing was in line with double-B ratings, although there was no country that easily compared with Jamaica.
"The deal has sold on the name rather than fundamentals," an emerging market debt trader said. "It sounds glamourous."
Pricing was expected at the low end of the indicated range.
Denmark and New Zealand also launched dollar deals, tapping into European retail demand for short-dated dollars.

Bankers said Denmark's $300 million four-year bond, priced to yield 15 b.p. over, looked "extremely cheap", and institutional accounts had bought the paper in anticipation of spread tightening once retail investors started buying.
New Zealand's $300 million three-year bond, priced to yield two b.p. over, was on the tight side but demand was boosted by the rarity of New Zealand in the market and a shortage of sovereign paper.
Next week, Canada is due to issue a dollar bond aimed at Japanese retail investors for up to $500 million, bankers said.
Dollar bonds aimed at institutional investors were unlikely to surface in the coming days, they said.
"Demand in the 10-year sector has dried up, and spreads are trading too expensively in the five-year sector to attract institutional interest," a syndicate manager at a European bank said.
